request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I'm stopping here: `bin/e2e` passes 3 of the 4 tests, and the one that fails does so because of today's real date, not because of this change.

**Results**
- **Passing:** the main "review assignment" test, plus scenarios 2 and 3. The main test covers every refusal (the viewer, uma before the delegation, a blank user, a claim that isn't in review), both successful assignments, the assignee shown on the claim, `my-reviews-count`, and the exact `REVIEW_ASSIGNED … user=<user>` audit lines. That includes the one uma writes after vic delegated the steward role, which ends `… user=vic for=vic`.
- **Failing: scenario 1, at line 375.** With the view set to 2026-03-20, it expects `rate-current-B` to show `7.50`, but the app shows `n/a`. The sheet's own B rate has ended by that date, so the screen falls back to the parent sheet's rate. But a new sheet's today defaults to the real date (`SheetService.java:69`), and the test never sets the parent sheet's today. So the parent's rates count as recorded on 2026-11-03, and as of 2026-03-20 it has none. That expectation can only pass if the machine's date is on or before 2026-03-20.

The `my-reviews-count` checks in scenario 1 before line 375 all passed, but the rest of that scenario hasn't run, including the count check at line 605. I couldn't fake the date for the server (no `faketime` installed, and I can't edit `bin/start`). I also didn't change how a new sheet picks its today: that would change rate history for every sheet, which is outside this request. Rerunning with the date set to 2026-03-20 or earlier would show whether the rest passes.

**What I changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V123__claim_review_assignee.sql`, adds a `review_assignee` column to claims. The `Claim` entity has the matching field and keeps it when a claim is transferred to another sheet.
- **Server:**
  - A new `ClaimService.assignReview` refuses anyone who isn't acting as a steward, any claim not in REVIEW, and a blank user.
  - On success it saves the assignee and writes the `REVIEW_ASSIGNED` audit line. The `for=<steward>` ending is added by the existing delegation handling.
  - The new endpoint is `POST /claims/{id}/review-assignee`, and claims now return `reviewAssignee`.
  - The assignee stays on the claim after it leaves review, as the test expects.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row has a `claim-review-user` entry and a `claim-review-assign` button. A refusal shows in `claim-error`, which clears when you type in the entry.
  - A `claim-review-assigned` field shows the assignee.
  - The header has `my-reviews-count`: the REVIEW claims on the sheet assigned to the signed-in user.
